_readme: Committed analyzer-warning baseline. .github/workflows/ci.yml gates every build
against it via tools/compare-warnings.ps1 (Windows runner) / tools/compare-warnings.sh.
The gate is a RATCHET: the total may fall, never rise, and a warning CODE absent
from this file fails the build. It never uses -warnaserror.
FORMATTING IS LOAD-BEARING for the .sh variant, which parses this file with awk
rather than jq: keep exactly one "CODE": N pair per line inside each "codes"
object, and keep "total" inside its target object. The .ps1 uses a real JSON
To update: see docs/kb/execution/ci-pipeline.md -> 'How to update the baseline'.

description: Count only the ': warning <CODE>:' lines that appear AFTER MSBuild's
'Build succeeded.' / 'Build FAILED.' marker -- i.e. MSBuild's own warning
summary block -- and assert that the resulting total equals the
'<n> Warning(s)' figure MSBuild prints in the same block. If the two
disagree, the gate exits 2 rather than gate on a number it cannot explain.
counting_rule.why_not_raw_line_count: Confirmed 2026-08-17 on this repository: the Api build log contained 13,386 raw ' warning <CODE>' lines against MSBuild's own 6,693 Warning(s) -- exactly 2x, because every diagnostic is printed once inline (node-prefixed, e.g. '2>') and once in the summary block.
counting_rule.why_not_divide_by_two: It reconciles today but is a magic number: it breaks silently the moment verbosity, node count or logger configuration changes.
counting_rule.why_not_text_deduplication: Measured WRONG here: the same log had 13,310 DISTINCT warning lines against 13,386 total, i.e. some diagnostics legitimately repeat with byte-identical text (up to 3x). Text de-duplication would under-count.
counting_rule.build_flags_assumed: --no-restore --no-incremental -v normal. An INCREMENTAL build reports fewer warnings than a cold one, so --no-incremental is required for the number to mean anything; -v normal is required for the summary block to exist.

provenance.runner_os: windows-11-developer-workstation (OS Version 10.0.26200) -- NOT a GitHub-hosted runner
note: M0-07 specifies that these numbers must be produced ON THE RUNNER. The
execution session that created this file could not push a branch (pushing is
not permitted from an execution session), so no GitHub Actions run could be
triggered and no runner measurement exists yet. These figures were measured
locally, with the exact commands and flags the workflow uses, so the workflow
is runnable and self-describing on its first run.
FIRST ACTION AFTER THIS BRANCH IS PUSHED: run the workflow, take the totals
and per-code counts it reports, replace the 'targets' blocks below with them,
set provenance.measured_on to the runner image, provisional to false, and
record the local-vs-runner delta in docs/kb/execution/ci-pipeline.md and in
INV-029. Where the two disagree, the RUNNER's number wins -- CI can only gate

delta_vs_KB086.explanation: KB-086 measured a plain 'dotnet build <csproj>' -- restore included. The CI pipeline runs restore as its OWN step (dotnet restore, then dotnet build --no-restore), which moves the restore-time NU1608 warnings out of the build log: Api loses 2 NU1608, Web loses 2 of 3 (one NU1608 is still emitted during Web's build). Confirmed by per-code arithmetic: KB-086 §5 groups every code below CS8767 into a 17-warning 'remaining' bucket including NU1608; the same codes measured here without NU1608 sum to 15. Everything else matches KB-086 §5 code for code.
